tldr: For the given natural indirect quantile curve, a single joint count, CDF and calibrated dyadic interval confidence image has finite-sample simultaneous coverage at least \(0.9\) over the full closed model. Its pointwise expected sup-width matches all-band lower bounds at every center with fixed interior slack. The evaluated scale combines the rare-path gradient and product term with \(\rho_n(w_n(P))\), where \(\rho_n(w)=\min\{w b_n,\sqrt{w\log(e/w)/n}\}\). The moving-interval geometry and its signed bump mixture prove that the maximum quantile gap suffices. Active cancellation retains the rare-path width scale. Under the separately established process theorem's fixed-primitive cancellation conditions its limit is Gaussian, while the simultaneous-null process has a product law with a learned common-density denominator.
